answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock stake subject to cryptographic stake burning when misbehavior is detected, driving an attacker's balance to its nadir. Registering concurrent identities incurs a superlinear cost scaling with degree $O(N^2)$, so adversaries cannot simply wander across unverified pseudonyms. Like a transient comet burning fuel rapidly, malicious swarms face quadratic slashing that renders large-scale identity spoofing mathematically unprofitable.
